context: The inputs are the traversals preorder = [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder = [9, 3, 1, 2, 7], with distinct node values.

Each recursive subproblem creates its root from the first element of the active preorder segment on descent. It splits the inorder segment at the root and recursively builds the left and right subtrees. Only when a child call returns its subtree root does the parent assign the current root’s left or right reference, creating the edge on return. A call on an empty interval returns None immediately.
description: Nine frames show nodes being created or subtrees being attached. Calls that return None for empty intervals have no separate frame. Each “Tree construction, step N” table lists all nodes and references created so far. “Unlinked” means the subtree still awaits construction or attachment on return. “None” means that child is absent.

frames.announcement: Create root 3 and separate the left subtree [9] from the three nodes of the right subtree.
frames.explanation: Enter the top-level call with i = 0 and inorder interval [0, 4]. Create root 3 from the first preorder value. Its inorder index is 1. The left subtree is [9], and the right subtree has inorder [1, 2, 7] and preorder [2, 1, 7]. Only root 3 exists, with no edges yet. Recurse into the left subtree first.
frames.key_state: Root 3 exists. Neither subtree is linked yet.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 1: nodes and references after creating root 3

frames.title: Create root 3

frames.announcement: Recurse into the left subproblem and create leaf 9, ready to return it.
frames.explanation: Enter the left subproblem with i = 1 and inorder interval [0, 0]. Create node 9. Both of its inorder subintervals are empty, so the corresponding calls return None, making 9 a leaf. The call building 9 has not yet returned it to root 3, so no edge joins the two nodes.
frames.key_state: Leaf 9 exists and is waiting to be linked to root 3.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 2: nodes and references after creating leaf 9

frames.title: Create leaf 9

frames.announcement: Attach the returned leaf 9 to the left of root 3.
frames.explanation: The call that built node 9 returns it to root 3. The parent call sets 3.left = 9, creating the first edge. The right subtree of root 3 remains to be built. Continue with the right subproblem.
frames.key_state: The edge 3.left = 9 is in place. The right subtree of root 3 still needs to be built.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 3: nodes and references after attaching left subtree 9

frames.title: Attach left subtree 9

frames.announcement: Create node 2 as the right subtree root and split its children into subproblems [1] and [7].
frames.explanation: Enter the right subproblem with i = 2 and inorder interval [2, 4]. Create node 2 from the first element of the active preorder segment [2, 1, 7]. Its inorder index is m = 3. Its left subproblem is [1] and its right subproblem is [7]. The edge 3.left = 9 remains. Neither child of 2 is linked, and the call rooted at 2 has not yet returned to 3, so there is no edge from 3 to 2.
frames.key_state: Node 2 exists, with both subtrees still to be built. The only edge is 3.left = 9, and 2 is still separate from 3.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 4: nodes and references after creating right subtree root 2

frames.title: Create right subtree root 2

frames.announcement: Create leaf 1, ready to return it to parent 2.
frames.explanation: Enter the left subproblem of node 2 with i = 3 and inorder interval [2, 2]. Create leaf 1. Both inorder subintervals are empty, but the call building node 1 has not yet returned it to node 2. Four nodes now exist. The only edge is 3.left = 9. Node 1 is still separate from 2, and 2 from 3.
frames.key_state: Leaf 1 exists. The only edge is 3.left = 9. Node 1 is still separate from 2, and 2 from 3.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 5: nodes and references after creating leaf 1

frames.title: Create leaf 1

frames.announcement: Attach the returned leaf 1 to the left of node 2.
frames.explanation: The call that built node 1 returns it to node 2. The parent call sets 2.left = 1. The edges are now 3.left = 9 and 2.left = 1. The right subproblem [7] still needs to be built, and node 2 has yet to return and attach to 3.
frames.key_state: The edges are 3.left = 9 and 2.left = 1. The subtree for 2.right still needs to be built, and 2 is still separate from 3.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 6: nodes and references after attaching the left subtree of node 2

frames.title: Attach the left subtree of node 2

frames.announcement: Create leaf 7, ready to return it to parent 2.
frames.explanation: Enter the right subproblem of node 2 with i = 4 and inorder interval [4, 4]. Create the last leaf, 7. All five nodes exist. The edges 3.left = 9 and 2.left = 1 are in place, while 2.right and 3.right are still unlinked. The call that built node 7 is about to return it to node 2.
frames.key_state: All five nodes exist. The edges are 3.left = 9 and 2.left = 1. The references 2.right and 3.right are still unlinked.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 7: nodes and references after creating leaf 7

frames.title: Create leaf 7

frames.announcement: Attach leaf 7 to the right of node 2, completing the subtree rooted at 2.
frames.explanation: The call that built node 7 returns it to node 2. The parent sets 2.right = 7. The three edges are now 3.left = 9, 2.left = 1, and 2.right = 7. The subtree rooted at 2 is complete and ready to return to root 3. No edge joins 3 and 2 yet.
frames.key_state: The edge 3.left = 9 is in place. The subtree rooted at 2 is complete, with left child 1 and right child 7, and is waiting to be linked to 3.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 8: nodes and references after attaching the right subtree of node 2

frames.title: Attach the right subtree of node 2

frames.announcement: Attach the completed subtree rooted at 2 to the right of root 3 and return root 3 to finish construction.
frames.explanation: The right subtree rooted at 2 returns to the top-level call, which sets 3.right = 2 to create the final edge. Node 3 has left child 9 and right child 2. Node 2 has left child 1 and right child 7. Nodes 9, 1, and 7 are leaves. With all four parent–child edges in place, the top-level function returns root 3 to finish construction.
frames.key_state: The tree is complete. Node 3 has left child 9 and right child 2. Node 2 has left child 1 and right child 7.

state_tables.caption: Tree construction, step 9: nodes and references after attaching the completed right subtree

frames.title: Attach the completed right subtree

result: The completed tree has preorder traversal [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder traversal [9, 3, 1, 2, 7], matching the input.
summary: Recursive descent creates nodes 3, 9, 2, 1, and 7 in order. As calls return, they link each subtree to its parent, completing the five-node tree.
title: Recursive tree construction: create nodes on descent and link subtrees on return
